stories.headline: Pavel-Babiš dispute over NATO Ankara summit delegation deepens, constitutional lawsuit threatened
stories.summary: An ongoing constitutional conflict between President Pavel and Prime Minister Babiš over who will represent Czechia at the July NATO summit in Ankara intensified this week. Pavel insists on his constitutional right to attend as head of state; Babiš argues the government delegation should not include the president. The government removed planned NATO-related flights from its official travel list, public opinion is split, and Pavel has not ruled out filing a competence lawsuit at the Constitutional Court. The president met with Deputy PM Havlíček on May 17 in a further attempt to resolve the dispute.

stories.headline: Coalition parliament passes resolution against Sudeten German assembly in Brno, damaging Czech-German relations
stories.summary: The coalition government of ANO, SPD, and Motoristé provoked a domestic and international row over the Sudeten German Landmannschaft's planned assembly in Brno (scheduled for 22–25 May). Speaker Okamura led a push for a parliamentary resolution expressing disapproval; an extraordinary session passed the resolution with coalition votes despite an nearly empty chamber. Critics, including commentators and former diplomats, condemned the move as harmful to Czech-German relations, while Okamura and Babiš faced accusations of political opportunism and inconsistency.

stories.headline: Public broadcaster media law draws cross-coalition criticism; nationwide protests erupt
stories.summary: A draft law on public media (Czech Television and Czech Radio), prepared by Culture Minister Klempíř of the Motorists, drew sharp criticism during an inter-ministerial review process — including from coalition partner Motorists and from broadcast unions. PM Babiš announced the coalition council would discuss the draft on 25 May. Simultaneously, thousands of protesters marched in multiple Czech cities (Brno, Olomouc, Hradec Králové and others) under the slogan 'Ruce pryč od médií' (Hands off the media) to defend public broadcasting from government intervention.

stories.headline: Czech defense spending push: government moves toward 2% GDP NATO target, army modernization debated
stories.summary: The Babiš government moved to reach the 2% GDP NATO defense spending target this year, with Defense Minister Zůna indicating a ~20 billion CZK top-up is needed. Babiš publicly questioned the metric of GDP percentages versus actual military capability (citing Luxembourg's small army), and the parliament's defense committee reviewed NATO commitment fulfillment. Separately, plans to create a robotic army battalion at Vyškov and the government's broader defense modernization trajectory were reported.

stories.headline: Parliament approves loosened budget rules over opposition criticism, opening path to higher deficits
stories.summary: The Chamber of Deputies approved an amendment to public budget laws despite strong opposition criticism. The legislation allows the government to increase spending on strategic infrastructure and defense above approved expenditure ceilings, with defense spending above 2% GDP excluded from deficit calculations through 2036. Opposition and fiscal watchdogs warned the change could allow deficits of up to 400 billion CZK in coming years; Babiš defended it as necessary and blamed the previous Fiala government for EU commitments that locked in a 150 billion deficit target.

stories.headline: French tax investigators close Babiš villa case; national financial prosecutor takes over
stories.summary: French specialist tax investigators concluded their multi-year probe into Czech Prime Minister Babiš's alleged purchase of a southern French property through offshore companies, a case originating from the Pandora Papers leak. The investigation into possible money laundering and tax fraud has been transferred to France's National Financial Prosecutor, which will decide on next steps. Babiš has consistently denied any wrongdoing.

stories.headline: Czech defense industry expands: CSG seeks KNDS stake, VOP gains NATO welding certification, drone contract with US Army
stories.summary: A cluster of Czech defense industry developments this week: Czech arms group CSG approached France and Germany with a proposal to acquire a stake in tank manufacturer KNDS; military repair enterprise VOP received a unique German certification enabling it to weld military vehicles for Rheinmetall and prepare for CV90 assembly; and Kolín-based drone maker U&C UAS signed a contract to supply reconnaissance drones to US Army units in Europe. President Pavel also appointed new generals on May 8.

stories.headline: Babiš halts Czech payments for Ukraine shell procurement pipeline while keeping program running
stories.summary: Reporting this week revealed that the Babiš government quietly stopped funding the Czech-led shell procurement program for Ukraine, relying instead on external donors to cover the full cost of the €5 billion 2026 target. The program, which has delivered 4.4 million large-caliber shells since 2024, continues to operate but with a reported €3.6 billion funding gap, according to Czech Ambassador to Ukraine Luboš Veselý.

stories.headline: Babiš ousts respected NATO expert from Defense Ministry; Šedivý departure linked to army budget transparency
stories.summary: Respekt reported that Jiří Šedivý, a well-regarded NATO affairs expert serving under Defense Minister Zůna, was forced out after PM Babiš objected to Šedivý's role in organizing an inter-ministerial briefing on the true state of the defense budget. Babiš reportedly summoned Zůna and demanded Šedivý's removal. The episode was cited as evidence of Babiš's personal interventions in defense policy.

stories.headline: Pavel and Babiš reach partial agreement on four ambassador nominations
stories.summary: President Pavel and Prime Minister Babiš agreed on changes to four ambassador nominations from the previous Fiala government's approved list. Pavel said he respects the new government's desire to post people it trusts in certain countries, but declined to name the specific posts involved. Ambassador appointments require presidential signature.
